The majority voted in favour of a [motion](http://www.openaustralia.org/debate/?id=2013-06-26.32.1) to read the bill a second time. This means that the majority of members agree with the main idea of the bill, which was "to enhance the Government’s ability to deter sponsor behaviour which is inconsistent with the policy intent of the Temporary Sponsored Visa Program (of which Subclass 457 visas are a part)".(Read more about the bill [here](http://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Bills_Legislation/Bills_Search_Results/Result?bId=r5068), which you can find its explanatory memorandum and bills digest. ) _Background to the Bill_ The [Migration Amendment (Temporary Sponsored Visas) Bill 2013](http://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Bills_Legislation/Bills_Search_Results/Result?bId=r5068) was introduced by Labor MP [Brendan O'Connor](http://publicwhip-rails.openaustraliafoundation.org.au/mp.php?mpn=Brendan_O%26%2339%3BConnor&mpc=Gorton&house=representatives) to “enhance the government's ability to deter sponsor behaviour which is inconsistent with the policy intent of the subclass 457 visa program and other temporary employer sponsored visa programs”.(Read MP O'Connor's comments [here](http://www.openaustralia.org/debates/?id=2013-06-06.3.2). ) At the time this bill was introduced, the [457 visa program](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/457_visa) was receiving extensive media attention with claims that it was being misused.(See [ABC News](http://www.abc.net.au/news/2013-06-02/an-457-crackdown/4728148). A simple explanation of the 457 visa scheme can be found on the Department of Immigration and Border Protection’s website [here](http://www.immi.gov.au/skilled/skilled-workers/sbs/).) References

The majority voted against a [motion](http://www.openaustralia.org/debate/?id=2013-06-26.44.1) moved by Liberal MP [Scott Morrison](http://publicwhip-rails.openaustraliafoundation.org.au/mp.php?mpn=Scott_Morrison&mpc=Cook&house=representatives). speeches.speaker: Scott Morrison
speeches.brief: Moved to suspend standing and sessional orders to delay debate on the Migration Amendment (Temporary Sponsored Visas) Bill 2013 until a full research report on 457 visa abuse, industry consultation, and a regulatory impact statement on the proposed labour market testing were completed, accusing the government of rushing the bill through for the unions before the election.

speeches.speaker: Scott Morrison
speeches.brief: Opposed the Migration Amendment (Temporary Sponsored Visas) Bill 2013 as a union-driven attack on skilled migration, citing department official Wendy Southern's evidence that no advice supported the minister's claim of 10,000 rorts, noting there were 108,810 primary 457 visa holders as at 30 April 2013, and quoting demographer Peter McDonald calling the Prime Minister's rhetoric on the issue nasty.

speeches.speaker: Tony Zappia
speeches.brief: Supported the 457 visa bill, describing a constituent tradesperson who lost a job to a 457 visa worker, cited figures showing 457 visa numbers rose from 68,400 in June 2010 to 106,680 in May 2013, a 56 per cent increase, and noted a Migration Council survey found 15 per cent of employers admitted they could have hired locally, while the bill extends the period for a displaced visa holder to find new work from 28 to 90 days.

speeches.speaker: Don Randall
speeches.brief: Called the 457 visa bill the most racist legislation he had encountered in parliament, comparing it to anti-Chinese hostility at the Lambing Flat goldfields riots 150 years earlier, and quoted the immigration minister's own maiden speech about not wanting his race to be an election issue.

speeches.speaker: Laurie Ferguson
speeches.brief: Accused the shadow minister for immigration of stoking ethnic division during debate on the Migration Amendment (Temporary Sponsored Visas) Bill 2013, after he warned a particular ethnic group would be victimised by a 457 visa crackdown having grown by 17 per cent through such visas, and recalled the shadow minister's earlier comments linking a rape case to refugee claimants.

speeches.speaker: Josh Frydenberg
speeches.brief: Opposed the Migration Amendment (Temporary Sponsored Visas) Bill 2013, accusing the union movement, which represents only 13 per cent of the private sector workforce, of controlling Labor Party policy, and defended 457 visa holders, noting more than 108,000 people held one as of April 2013 and 70 per cent worked in professional or managerial roles.

speeches.speaker: Alan Tudge
speeches.brief: Opposed the Migration Amendment (Temporary Sponsored Visas) Bill 2013, arguing it was rushed through to please the union movement and to distract from a chaotic border protection regime, contrasting the government's swift action on 457 visas with its months-long inaction on the Houston inquiry's recommendation to excise the mainland.

speeches.speaker: Alan Tudge
speeches.brief: Opposed the Migration Amendment (Temporary Sponsored Visas) Bill, disputing the immigration minister's unsubstantiated claim of 10,000 rorted 457 visas, noting union leader Tony Sheldon reported only 24 complaints in 12 months with none referred to the department, and said 457 visa numbers had risen by just 1.7 per cent over the past year.

speeches.speaker: Dan Tehan
speeches.brief: Opposed the migration bill, calling it the 'City West Water Bill' after a union picket over 457 visa workers at a Werribee water project, noted 24 complaints in 12 months with none referred to the immigration department, and praised former minister Chris Bowen for intervening to let a group of Chinese 457 workers stay in Warrnambool after more than five years at a local abattoir.

speeches.speaker: Janelle Saffin
speeches.brief: Supported the migration bill, citing a Migration Council survey finding 15 per cent of employers used 457 visas despite reporting no difficulty finding local labour, and pointed to the Northern Co-operative Meat Co. abattoir in the Page electorate, which employs nearly a thousand workers, as a model combining 457 visas with local training.

speeches.speaker: Bob Baldwin
speeches.brief: Opposed the migration bill as hypocritical, citing a 2011 joint press release from Labor's own tourism and immigration ministers acknowledging a tourism skills shortage needing 457 visas, and said Labor had cut compliance funding for 457 monitoring by more than $20 million, a 30 per cent reduction, in government.

speeches.speaker: Robert Oakeshott
speeches.brief: Announced opposition to the migration bill, arguing existing sponsorship obligations already carry penalties of up to AUD51,000 per breach for a corporation, and said a 20 per cent rise in 457 visas against about 1.1 per cent growth in the construction industry was not evidence of rorting, only of laws needing to be enforced rather than replaced.

speeches.speaker: Alex Hawke
speeches.brief: Opposed the 457 visa bill, noting the program was introduced by the Howard government in 1996 to address skills shortages, said the minister could not substantiate his claim of 10,000 abuse cases, and cited figures showing India accounted for about 20.5 per cent of 457 visa grants in 2012-13.

speeches.speaker: Michael McCormack
speeches.brief: Opposed the 457 visa bill on behalf of Riverina farmers, citing grain grower Mark Hoskinson's reliance on French agricultural students for his harvest, and noted the bill would extend the period for a displaced 457 worker to find new sponsorship from 28 to 98 days while new compliance inspectors would cost $3.4 million.

speeches.speaker: Craig Kelly
speeches.brief: Opposed the 457 visa bill, saying the minister admitted plucking his claimed 10,000 abuse cases from thin air, cited a joint industry letter from the Australian Industry Group, Business Council of Australia and Migration Council Australia warning against the changes, and said 12,700 people had arrived by unauthorised boat this year, three times the same period last year, bringing the total under Labor to more than 44,600.

speeches.speaker: Jamie Briggs
speeches.brief: Opposed the 457 visa bill, noting the government could face an election in 86 days, recounted how then immigration minister Chris Bowen approved a migration agreement for a Gina Rinehart mining project, and said the South Australian Labor government was reportedly the state's biggest user of 457 visas.

speeches.speaker: Paul Fletcher
speeches.brief: Opposed the 457 visa bill as a protectionist measure driven by the union movement, citing CFMEU official Dave Noonan's claim that the proportion of 457 visas granted onshore had grown from 43 per cent to 51 per cent in a year, noted labour market testing was tried from 1996 and dropped by the Howard government in 2001 as unworkable, and said the minister's claim of 10,000 abuse cases remained unsubstantiated.

speeches.speaker: Steve Irons
speeches.brief: Opposed the 457 visa bill, reading a constituent's email from Bicycle Entrepreneur owner Michael D'Arcy in Belmont describing his inability to source bicycle mechanics locally, noted the WA government was lobbying for 16,500 regional sponsored visas, and compared the changes to the 2007-08 weakening of border protection that preceded more than 40,000 boat arrivals and over 1,000 deaths at sea.

speeches.speaker: Steve Irons
speeches.brief: Opposed the Migration Amendment (Temporary Sponsored Visas) Bill 2013, citing a Freedom of Information finding that the immigration minister had no evidence for a claimed 10,000 rorts of the 457 visa scheme, noted Western Australia's 457 applications fell 6.4 per cent in 2012 to 2013, and criticised extending the job-seeking period from 28 to 90 days as unhelpful red tape.

speeches.speaker: Sharman Stone
speeches.brief: Opposed the bill, describing how 457 visa holders from the Philippines have revitalised piggeries and schools around Yarrawalla in northern Victoria, and said about 30 or 40 per cent of skilled migrants historically went on to become Australian citizens under the coalition, disputing claims the visa system was being widely rorted.

speeches.speaker: Luke Hartsuyker
speeches.brief: Opposed the bill, recalling only four people were in immigration detention when Labor was elected in 2007, and said since 2008 more than 700 boats carrying over 44,200 people have arrived illegally, at a cost exceeding $10 billion to taxpayers.

speeches.speaker: Jane Prentice
speeches.brief: Argued that the Migration Amendment (Temporary Sponsored Visas) Bill 2013 was based on a false premise and would burden employers through labour-market testing and increased compliance requirements. Supported skilled temporary migration, called for evidence, consultation and a regulatory impact statement, and said the coalition would oppose the bill and seek committee referral.

speeches.speaker: Teresa Gambaro
speeches.brief: Argued that the Migration Amendment (Temporary Sponsored Visas) Bill 2013 would impose unnecessary regulation on employers, lacked evidence of widespread abuse, and threatened Australia's skilled migration program. Supported the 457 visa scheme as vital for addressing skills gaps, criticised labour-market testing, and said the bill risked dividing Australians and undermining economic growth.

speeches.speaker: Warren Entsch
speeches.brief: Argued that the bill would add unnecessary regulation to the 457 visa program and was not supported by evidence of widespread abuse. Cited regional skills shortages and problems affecting businesses, supported extending the period to find new sponsored employment from 28 days to 90 days, and said the coalition would oppose the bill.
